labeler: AI reviewer (Claude), a session separate from the one that wrote the rules. Not yet spot-checked by the maintainer.
method: Each repository was fetched at the pinned commit and read, never executed. Every finding location was checked against the source line, then judged by rule. Labels: correct = the claim is accurate and concerns code or instructions that run on a user machine; correct-nonruntime = accurate, but only in tests, CI or developer tooling; incorrect = the claim is factually wrong for that line; not-reviewed = not independently verifiable here.
limits: One reviewer, one pass. Labels for the largest repository were assigned by pattern after reading every flagged line, not by 224 separate hand judgments. "missed" is a spot check from grepping for common patterns, not an exhaustive search, so no recall figure can be derived from it.

missed.what: A 14 MB prebuilt ELF binary is committed to the repository and is run at every login by the systemd user unit that install.sh enables. The report verdict is "minor-notes" with highest severity low; the binary appears only in coverage.unknown as "too large". A shipped opaque executable wired to persistence should be a prominent finding.
cp deploy/starlinkd.service into ~/.config/systemd/user is the actual unit install and is not flagged (only the enable on line 29 is).

Installs a root-owned helper to /usr/local/bin, a polkit policy under /usr/share/polkit-1/actions and, with --passwordless, a polkit rule in /etc/polkit-1/rules.d that lets the user run the root helper without a password. Elevation goes through "${elevate[@]}" (sudo or pkexec) running bash -c. No finding at all was produced for this file.
tests/browser.test.cjs, dev/agent_smoke.py and browser/extension/background.js are reported as shell files with parse errors; they are JavaScript and Python.

The shipped installer downloads an AppImage with curl, marks it executable and runs it with --appimage-extract. Only the copy of this logic inside a markdown spec was flagged; the real script was not. (The real script does prompt before first execution, which would justify a lower severity, not silence.)
